1.title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud
1.text: Welcome to Module eight: Microsoft Defender for Cloud. It covers the exam area Capabilities of Microsoft security solutions. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Describe cloud security posture management (C S P M). Describe Microsoft Defender for Cloud. Describe security policies and standards. Describe security recommendations. Describe cloud workload protection. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Capabilities of Microsoft security solutions (thirty-five to forty percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official S C nine hundred study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-one, two thousand twenty-six.

1.title: What Defender for Cloud is
1.text: What Defender for Cloud is. Microsoft Defender for Cloud is a cloud-native application protection platform (C N A P P) that does two jobs. Find and fix weaknesses. Name: Cloud security posture management (C S P M). Question it answers: Is my environment configured securely? Detect and stop threats. Name: Cloud workload protection (C W P), delivered by Defender plans. Question it answers: Are my workloads under attack right now? It protects Azure, on-premises servers and other clouds such as A W S and Google Cloud (multicloud).

1.title: What Defender for Cloud is, continued
1.text: What Defender for Cloud is. The figure shows this: Defender for Cloud: posture management finds weaknesses, workload protection stops threats. Exam tip: C S P M (cloud security posture management) equals posture (misconfiguration, recommendations, secure score). Workload protection equals threats (alerts and defenses per resource type). Defender for Cloud covers multicloud and hybrid, not Azure only.

1.title: Cloud security posture management (CSPM)
1.text: Cloud security posture management (C S P M). Secure score. A percentage showing how well you follow security recommendations; higher is better. Security recommendations. Prioritized, actionable steps to fix weaknesses. Regulatory compliance dashboard. Shows how you measure against standards. Asset inventory. One view of all resources and their security state. Attack path analysis and cloud security graph. Shows how an attacker could reach critical assets (Defender C S P M plan). Governance rules. Assign owners and due dates to recommendations. Free foundational C S P M is included for Azure; Defender C S P M is the paid plan with advanced features.

1.title: Security recommendations
1.text: Security recommendations. A recommendation tells you what to fix, why, and how. Each shows severity, affected resources and remediation steps, and many offer Quick fix or Fix buttons. Examples: enable M F A for accounts, close management ports on V Ms, enable encryption, apply system updates. Recommendations are generated by security policies and standards that are assessed continuously. Secure score rises as you fix them.

1.title: Security policies and standards
1.text: Security policies and standards. Security policy. A rule about how resources should be configured (built on Azure Policy). Initiative. A group of policies assigned together. Standard. A set of controls from a benchmark or regulation. Microsoft cloud security benchmark (M C S B). The default standard, Microsoft's security best practices for Azure and multicloud. Regulatory standards. For example I S O twenty-seven thousand one, P C I D S S, nist S P eight hundred to fifty-three, S O C two can be added.

1.title: Security policies and standards, continued
1.text: Security policies and standards. The figure shows this: Policies and standards produce recommendations, which raise secure score when fixed. Exam tip: Policies and standards define what is expected; recommendations tell you what to do; secure score shows progress. The default standard is the Microsoft cloud security benchmark.

1.title: Cloud workload protection (Defender plans)
1.text: Cloud workload protection (Defender plans). Each Defender plan protects a resource type with threat detection and alerts. Defender for Servers. Virtual machines and servers (Azure, on-premises, other clouds); includes vulnerability assessment and endpoint protection with Defender for Endpoint. Defender for Storage. Storage accounts: malware scanning, unusual access. Defender for Databases (sequel, open-source databases, Cosmos D B). Databases: sequel injection and anomalous access. Defender for App Service. Web apps. Defender for Key Vault. Key vault misuse. Defender for Containers. Kubernetes and container images. Defender for Resource Manager. Suspicious management operations. Defender for A P Is. A P I threats.

1.title: Cloud workload protection (Defender plans), continued
1.text: Cloud workload protection (Defender plans). Key points: plans are enabled per subscription, are paid by resource, and raise security alerts with recommended responses; alerts can be sent to Microsoft Sentinel and the Defender X D R portal. Exam tip: "Detect attacks on virtual machines, databases or storage" equals a Defender plan (workload protection). "Score and recommendations about configuration" equals C S P M.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants a percentage that shows how well its Azure resources follow security recommendations. What is it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Secure score. Secure score in Defender for Cloud measures posture against recommendations.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which Defender for Cloud capability detects an attack on a sequel database? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Cloud workload protection with a Defender plan. Defender plans provide threat detection for specific workloads such as databases.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. What is the default security standard in Defender for Cloud? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Microsoft cloud security benchmark. The Microsoft cloud security benchmark is the default standard.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A team wants guidance on which settings to change to improve security, with severity and remediation steps. Which feature gives this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Security recommendations. Recommendations are prioritized, actionable remediation guidance.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which statement about Defender for Cloud is true? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: It protects Azure, on-premises and other clouds. Defender for Cloud covers multicloud and hybrid environments.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which term describes a group of policies assigned together? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Initiative. An initiative bundles several policies.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does C S P M stand for? Answer: Cloud security posture management. Question two. What does secure score show? Answer: How well you follow security recommendations; higher is better. Question three. What do Defender plans provide? Answer: Cloud workload protection: threat detection and alerts per resource type.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Name the default standard. Answer: Microsoft cloud security benchmark. Question five. Which Azure service do Defender for Cloud policies build on? Answer: Azure Policy. Question six. Which paid plan adds attack path analysis? Answer: Defender C S P M.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Defender for Cloud: C N A P P; C S P M plus cloud workload protection; Azure, on-premises, multicloud. C S P M: secure score, recommendations, compliance dashboard, inventory, attack paths (Defender C S P M). Policies and standards: Azure Policy based; initiatives; default Microsoft cloud security benchmark; add I S O, P C I, nist. Workload protection: Defender for Servers, Storage, Databases, App Service, Key Vault, Containers, Resource Manager, A P Is. In the next module, we continue the course.
